ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a hexagram shape, pieced together from equilateral triangles of the same size. The central gray part is a hexagon; it can be seen that it is divided by internal line segments into 6 congruent small equilateral triangles; outside the hexagon there are also 6 white equilateral triangles forming the pointed corners of the star. The outer boundary of the star shape is composed of the exposed sides of these outer triangles, with a total of 12 small triangle sides. Reasoning: Let the side length of each small equilateral triangle be s. The perimeter of the star shape is 12s, and the problem gives it as 36 cm, so 12s = 36, obtaining s = 3 cm. The gray hexagon has 6 sides, each side is equal to the side length of one small triangle, therefore the perimeter of the gray hexagon is 6s = 6 × 3 = 18 cm.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the grey central hexagon is tiled by 6 of the congruent equilateral triangles, and the outer star boundary is made of the exposed sides of the 6 surrounding triangles. Let the common side length of each small equilateral triangle be s. Count from the image that the star outline consists of 12 small triangle sides, so 12s = 36 and s = 3 cm. The grey hexagon has 6 sides, each one small triangle side, so its perimeter is 6s = 18 cm.

method.method_draft: View the picture as a grey hexagon with one congruent equilateral triangle attached to each of its 6 sides. In the image, each attached outer triangle has its base hidden along one side of the grey hexagon and its other two equal sides exposed on the star boundary. If one grey hexagon side is s, each outer triangle contributes 2s to the star perimeter, so the whole star perimeter is 6 · 2s = 12s. Since this equals 36 cm, s = 3 cm. The grey hexagon perimeter is 6s = 18 cm.
